mainTopic: How the הלכה was fixed like בית הלל on סמיכה, the debate over bringing offerings on יום טוב, and what to do if a נדר or נדבה was slaughtered on יום טוב.
overview: This amud finishes the story of בבא בן בוטא, who filled the עזרה with sheep so that everyone would do סמיכה on יום טוב. That day the הלכה was fixed like בית הלל. In a later story, a student of בית הלל silences a student of בית שמאי, and אביי learns that you should never answer back more harshly than you were spoken to. Next comes a ברייתא in which בית הלל and בית שמאי debate whether offerings may be brought on יום טוב. The two sides argue with a קל וחומר, with the example of נדרים ונדבות, with the question of whether the עולת ראייה has a fixed time, and with the פסוקים "לכם" and "לה׳". אבא שאול gives בית הלל's argument in a different version. The גמרא explains that the two versions disagree about whether נדרים ונדבות may be offered on יום טוב, and רב הונא says that the forbidding view treats this as a Torah prohibition. רבא and רבה בר רב הונא then argue over why the blood may be sprinkled if someone slaughtered such an offering anyway. The amud ends with an objection from the ברייתא of the כבשי עצרת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בבא בן בוטא brings sheep and the הלכה is set like בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: בבא בן בוטא fills the עזרה with sheep and invites everyone to do סמיכה. That day בית הלל win, and the הלכה is fixed like them with no one objecting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he brought all the fine Kedar sheep in Jerusalem and stood them in the Temple courtyard. He said: Whoever wants to lean his hands on an animal, let him come and lean. On that day בית הלל gained the upper hand, and they fixed the הלכה like them. No one there disputed the matter at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that began on the previous daf: בבא בן בוטא makes sure the public practice of סמיכה on יום טוב follows בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that you may not do סמיכה on an offering on יום טוב, and בית הלל hold that you may. By bringing many animals and inviting the crowd, בבא בן בוטא turned בית הלל's view into the accepted public practice. The phrase "no one disputed" tells us the הלכה was now settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine, high-quality sheep from the region of Kedar
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
Leaning one's hands with force on an animal's head before it is offered
Their hand became stronger, meaning they won the dispute
Objected or disputed

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this story begins here. It started on the previous daf. The "he" who brought the sheep is בבא בן בוטא, a student of בית שמאי who knew the הלכה was like בית הלל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the הלכה came to follow בית הלל on the question of סמיכה on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And he brought all the Kedar sheep that were in Jerusalem
phrases.notes: "He" is בבא בן בוטא, from the story on the previous daf.

phrases.english: and stood them in the Temple courtyard,
and said: Anyone who wishes to lean his hands —
let him come and lean,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם גָּבְרָה יָדָן שֶׁל בֵּית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: and on that day Beit Hillel gained the upper hand
and they established the halacha like them,
and there was no person there
who disputed the matter in any way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the בבא בן בוטא story from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה was fixed like בית הלל: סמיכה is done on offerings on יום טוב.

steps.title: A בית הלל student silences a בית שמאי student
steps.stepSummary: Later, a student of בית שמאי challenges a student of בית הלל who is doing סמיכה on יום טוב. The בית הלל student answers "What is this silence?" and silences him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another incident: a student of בית הלל brought his burnt-offering to the courtyard to lean his hands on it. A student of בית שמאי found him and said: What is this leaning? He answered: What is this silence? He silenced him with a rebuke, and the other went away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second, later story showing that once the הלכה was settled, a challenge from בית שמאי's side was simply shut down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בית שמאי student objects to doing סמיכה on יום טוב. The בית הלל student replies that he should keep quiet, since the הלכה has already been decided. The rebuke works, and the challenger leaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Another incident, a further story
Burnt-offering, which is burned entirely on the מזבח
Silence
A rebuke or scolding

phrases.english: Again there was an incident with a certain student
from the students of Beit Hillel
who brought his burnt-offering to the Temple courtyard
to lean his hands on it,

phrases.aramaic: מְצָאוֹ תַּלְמִיד אֶחָד מִתַּלְמִידֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי,
phrases.english: a certain student from the students of Beit Shammai found him,
he said to him: What is this leaning?
He said to him: What is this silence?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why aren't you staying quiet, since the הלכה is already settled?

phrases.english: He silenced him with a rebuke, and he went away.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּתַלְמִיד אֶחָד מִתַּלְמִידֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up story showing the settled הלכה in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the הלכה was fixed, an objection against סמיכה on יום טוב was rejected.

steps.title: אביי: Don't answer back harsher than you were spoken to
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from the story that a תלמיד חכם who is challenged should not answer back more strongly than the challenge itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Therefore, a Torah scholar whose colleague says something to him should not answer back more than what his colleague said to him. For that one said, "What is this leaning?" and the other answered, "What is this silence?"
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a lesson about good manners from the story: when someone criticizes you, answer in the same measure and no more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בית הלל student matched the challenger exactly: "מה זו" was answered with "מה זו," using the same short phrasing. אביי sees this as a model, because answering back harsher only makes the fight bigger.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
A young Torah scholar
To answer back, to reply
More

steps.whatToRemember: From these stories: the הלכה follows בית הלל on סמיכה on יום טוב, and אביי teaches never to answer back more harshly than you were spoken to.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a lasting lesson in how Torah scholars should behave toward each other.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Therefore,
a Torah scholar
whose colleague says something to him,
should not answer him back with something
more than what his colleague said to him,
for that one said to him: "What is this leaning?"
and he answered him: "What is this silence?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a moral lesson from the story in Step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not answer back more than what was said to you.

steps.title: בית הלל's קל וחומר for offerings on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל argue with a קל וחומר: on שבת, slaughtering for people is forbidden, yet offerings for הקב"ה are allowed. So on יום טוב, when slaughtering for people is allowed, offerings for הקב"ה should surely be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: If in a place where slaughtering for an ordinary person is forbidden, it is still permitted for the Most High, then in a place where it is permitted for an ordinary person, isn't it logical that it is permitted for the Most High?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with בית הלל's logical proof that offerings, such as עולות ראייה, may be brought on יום טוב. This opens a back-and-forth with בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "place where it is forbidden for a person" is שבת: you may not slaughter for food, but the תמיד and מוסף are offered. The "place where it is permitted for a person" is יום טוב, where slaughtering for food is allowed. If the stricter day still allows offerings, the more lenient day should allow them too.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
An ordinary person, as opposed to the Temple
The Most High, meaning offerings for הקב"ה
Is it not logical? This phrase signals a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: "Place" here means a time, not a physical location. "מקום שאסור" is שבת, and "מקום שמותר" is יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: It was taught: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
Just as in a place where it is forbidden for an ordinary person —
it is permitted for the Most High,
phrases.notes: The תמיד and מוסף are offered on שבת.

phrases.english: then a place where it is permitted for an ordinary person —
is it not logical that it is permitted for the Most High?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section: a ברייתא with the logical debate behind the מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: That offerings such as עולות ראייה may be brought on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from שבת, where offerings are allowed even though slaughtering for people is not.

steps.title: בית שמאי: Vow and gift offerings disprove the argument
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי reject the קל וחומר with a counter-example: נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב, even though slaughtering for people is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: Vow-offerings and gift-offerings prove otherwise. On יום טוב it is permitted to slaughter for an ordinary person, yet these offerings are forbidden for the Most High!
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי knock down בית הלל's logic by pointing to a case where the קל וחומר clearly does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר claimed that whenever slaughtering for people is allowed, offerings must be allowed too. בית שמאי point to נדרים ונדבות, which are not brought on יום טוב even though people may slaughter for food that day. So the rule "allowed for people, therefore allowed for הקב"ה" is not reliable.

keyTerms.meaning: Vow-offerings, where a person said "I take upon myself to bring an offering"
Gift-offerings, where a person said "this animal is an offering"
They will prove, used to bring a counter-example

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:
Vow-offerings and gift-offerings will prove,
that it is permitted for an ordinary person yet forbidden for the Most High!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר from Step 4 with a counter-example.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר of בית הלל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being allowed for people does not automatically make something allowed for הקב"ה, as נדרים ונדבות show.

steps.title: בית הלל: Vow and gift offerings have no fixed time
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer בית שמאי's counter-example. נדרים ונדבות have no fixed time, so they can wait until after יום טוב. An עולת ראייה has a fixed time, so it is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: Why are נדרים ונדבות not brought on יום טוב? Because they have no set time. Can you say the same about an עולת ראייה, which does have a set time?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל defend their קל וחומר. They show that בית שמאי's counter-example of נדרים ונדבות does not fit the case of an עולת ראייה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נדרים ונדבות can be brought on any weekday, so there is no reason to bring them on יום טוב. An עולת ראייה belongs to the festival itself, so it needs to be brought then. That difference removes the force of בית שמאי's counter-example.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings a person chooses to pledge (a נדר) or donate (a נדבה). They are not tied to any date.
It has a fixed, set time.
The burnt-offering brought when appearing in the בית המקדש on the רגל.
'What about...?' A formula that points out how one case is different from another.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בית הלל agree that nothing may be offered on יום טוב. They are only explaining why נדרים ונדבות are an exception. That exception does not apply to an offering that has its own set time.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them:
What about vow-offerings and gift-offerings?
They have no fixed time.
Will you say the same about a burnt-offering of appearance,
which has a fixed time?
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question. The point is that you cannot compare the two.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לִנְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לָהֶם זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's counter-example from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (fixed time versus no fixed time).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב, no offering for ה׳ should be.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only offerings with no fixed time are left out. An offering tied to the festival may be brought.

steps.title: בית שמאי: The appearance offering can also be pushed off
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי argue that an עולת ראייה also has no truly fixed time. A משנה says that if someone did not bring it on the first day of סוכות, he may bring it on any later day of the חג.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: This one also has no fixed time. As we learned: someone who did not bring his festival offering on the first day of the חג may keep bringing it the whole festival, including the last day of the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push back on בית הלל's distinction. They quote a משנה to show that an עולת ראייה can be delayed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the offering can be brought on any day of the festival, it does not have to be brought on יום טוב itself. It could wait for a חול המועד day. So, like נדרים ונדבות, there is no need to bring it on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: This one too.
As we learned in a משנה.
Here it means 'brought his festival offering.'
He may keep bringing it as the days go on.
Pilgrimage festival.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אַף זוֹ אֵין קָבוּעַ לָהּ זְמַן,
phrases.english: This one too has no fixed time,
as we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁלֹּא חָג בְּיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג —
phrases.english: One who did not bring his festival offering on the first festival day of Sukkot
may continue to bring it throughout the entire festival,
and on the last festival day of the holiday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף זוֹ אֵין קָבוּעַ לָהּ זְמַן דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the distinction בית הלל made in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that an עולת ראייה has a fixed time.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The offering can be delayed to other days, so it does not need to be brought on יום טוב.

steps.title: בית הלל: Its time is still limited to the festival
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that the עולת ראייה still has a fixed time, even if that time is longer. Once the whole festival passes, the obligation is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: This one also has a fixed time. As we learned: if the festival passed and he did not bring his offering, he is not responsible for it anymore.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל defend their distinction with another משנה. That משנה shows the offering is tied to the festival period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'fixed time' is the whole festival, not one single day. נדרים ונדבות can be brought at any time of the year. The עולת ראייה expires when the חג ends, so it really is a time-bound offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival has passed.
He is not responsible to make it up.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them:
This one too has a fixed time.
As we learned in a mishna:
If the festival passed and he did not bring his festival offering,
he is not accountable for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף זוֹ קָבוּעַ לָהּ זְמַן דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's objection in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining 'fixed time' as the whole festival period.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the offering can be delayed, it has no fixed time.
steps.terutzMaskana: It has a longer fixed time, the whole festival, and expires after that. It is still different from נדרים ונדבות.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'fixed time' debate ends with בית הלל's point: an offering limited to the festival counts as time-bound, even if it can be brought on any day of that festival.

steps.title: בית שמאי: The verse says 'for you,' not for the Most High
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי switch from logic to a פסוק. The Torah allows food preparation on יום טוב "לכם" (for you), which suggests it is not allowed for offerings to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: Wasn't it already said, "for you"? That means for you, and not for the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי bring a proof from a פסוק that offerings for ה׳ should not be prepared on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission to do מלאכה for food on יום טוב comes from the words "לכם". בית שמאי read that word as limiting the permission to human needs only, so it does not include sacrifices.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it already stated?
For you (from שמות יב:טז).
The Most High, meaning ה׳. Here it refers to offerings.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:
But wasn't it already stated:
"For you" — and not for the Most High.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר לָכֶם וְלֹא לְגָבוֹהַּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'fixed time' logic debate and brings a proof from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That offerings may not be brought on יום טוב.

steps.title: בית הלל: The verse says 'to ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer with their own פסוק: the festival is "לה׳" (to ה׳), which includes everything offered to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: Wasn't it already said, "to ה׳"? That means anything that is for ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל answer one פסוק with another. Theirs supports bringing offerings on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "לה׳" show that the festival is celebrated for ה׳. That includes the offerings brought to Him. Now there are two פסוקים that seem to point in opposite directions, and the next step explains how they fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: To ה׳ (from ויקרא כג:מא).
Anything that is for ה׳.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them:
But wasn't it already stated:
"To the Lord" — anything that is for the Lord.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר לַה׳ כֹּל דְּלַה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's פסוק with a different פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That offerings may be brought on יום טוב.

steps.title: בית הלל explain 'for you': not for gentiles or dogs
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל explain what "לכם" really excludes: cooking on יום טוב for גוים or for dogs, not cooking for ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say "for you"? For you, and not for gentiles. For you, and not for dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל take away בית שמאי's proof by giving the word "לכם" a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since "לה׳" already includes offerings, "לכם" cannot be excluding them. It must be excluding other things instead: preparing food on יום טוב for a גוי or for animals. That way both פסוקים fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: If so.
What does the פסוק come to teach by saying this?
Non-Jews.
Dogs.

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying "for you"?
For you — and not for gentiles;
for you — and not for dogs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes בית הלל's reply by reinterpreting בית שמאי's פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: "לכם" excludes cooking for גוים and dogs, and offerings to ה׳ stay permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that one may not cook on יום טוב for a גוי or for animals.

steps.title: אבא שאול: If ה׳'s stove is open on שבת, surely on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול gives בית הלל's קל וחומר in a different form. Your stove is closed on שבת, yet ה׳'s stove (the מזבח) is open. On יום טוב your stove is open, so surely His is too. It would not be fitting for your table to be full while your Master's table is empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול said it another way: On שבת your stove is closed, yet your Master's stove is open. On יום טוב your stove is open, so isn't it logical that your Master's stove is open too? It also makes sense that your table should not be full while your Master's table is empty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings אבא שאול's version of בית הלל's argument. It is the same קל וחומר, told with a picture of two stoves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'stove' stands for cooking. On שבת you may not cook, but the מזבח is still in use. On יום טוב you may cook for yourself, so the מזבח should surely be in use too. He adds a point about fairness and respect: a servant should not eat a full meal while his Master's table, the מזבח, stays empty.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who reports the argument in a different version.
In a different wording.
Stove.
Closed (not allowed) / open (allowed).
Isn't it logical? The wording of a קל וחומר.
Your Master's table, meaning the מזבח.

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's main argument is a קל וחומר from שבת to יום טוב. אבא שאול puts it as a picture: if ה׳'s 'stove' is open when yours is closed, it is surely open when yours is open.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul states it in a different formulation:
Just as where your stove is closed (Shabbat),
your Master's stove is open,
then where your stove is open (Yom Tov),
is it not logical that your Master's stove should be open?
And it likewise stands to reason
that your table should not be full
while your Master's table is empty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of בית הלל's קל וחומר from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That offerings may be brought on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from שבת (the מזבח works even when private cooking is forbidden), plus a point about respect for the Master's table.

steps.title: What is the real disagreement between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what point divides the first ברייתא from אבא שאול's version of the debate.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask what the two versions of the debate (the first ברייתא and אבא שאול's version) are really arguing about. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, בית שמאי use נדרים ונדבות as a proof against בית הלל. אבא שאול's version does not use that argument. The גמרא wants to know which underlying issue causes this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: In what do they disagree? (asking for the root of a dispute)

phrases.english: In what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" = the תנא of the first ברייתא and אבא שאול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing אבא שאול's alternate version in Step 12, the גמרא asks what separates it from the first version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying point of dispute between the two versions of בית הלל's position.

steps.title: The dispute is whether vow and gift offerings may be brought on a festival
steps.stepSummary: One view holds נדרים ונדבות may be offered on יום טוב. The other holds they may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds that vow-offerings and gift-offerings may be brought on יום טוב, and the other Sage holds they may not be brought on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The two versions disagree about whether נדרים ונדבות may be offered on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול holds that, according to בית הלל, they may be offered, so בית שמאי could not use them as a proof. The first ברייתא holds they may not be offered, so בית שמאי could point to them as a proof. The disagreement between the versions grows out of this one question.

keyTerms.meaning: Vow-offerings, where a person says "I take upon myself to bring an offering"
Gift-offerings, where a person says "this animal is an offering"
One Sage holds... and the other Sage holds

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions agree about the עולת ראייה. The argument here is only about voluntary offerings (נדרים ונדבות), which do not have to be brought on the festival.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת קְרֵבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: vow-offerings and gift-offerings are brought on a festival,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר: אֵין קְרֵבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: they are not brought on a festival.
phrases.notes: This is the תנא of the first ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The versions disagree over whether נדרים ונדבות may be offered on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב הונא: the ban on vow and gift offerings is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that, according to the forbidding view, the ban is not a rabbinic fence against delay. It is a Torah prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: According to the one who says vow-offerings and gift-offerings are not brought on יום טוב, do not say that by Torah law they are fit, and only the Rabbis decreed against them so that a person would not delay his vow. Rather, even by Torah law they are not fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains how strong the forbidding opinion is. First he rejects a possible reason (a rabbinic decree), and then he states the real one: the Torah itself forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the Torah allows these offerings and the Rabbis only banned them so people would not push off their vows until the festival, which is a sin of delay. רב הונא says no: this opinion holds the Torah itself does not allow them on יום טוב. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
A rabbinic decree, a protective fence
Lest he delay (bringing his promised offering)
Do not say... rather (rejects one reading and gives the correct one)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
According to the one who says vow-offerings and gift-offerings
are not brought on a festival,
do not say: by Torah law they are fit,
and it is the Rabbis who decreed about them
phrases.notes: That they should not be brought on the festival.

phrases.english: as a decree lest he delay,
phrases.notes: He might push off his vow until the festival, when he is already at the Temple, and break the rule against delaying vows.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא נָמֵי לָא חָזוּ.
phrases.english: rather, even by Torah law they are also not fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how strong the forbidding opinion from Step 14 is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the forbidding view, offering נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב is forbidden by Torah law, not only by a rabbinic decree.

steps.title: Proof from the שתי הלחם of שבועות
steps.stepSummary: The שתי הלחם are an obligation of the day, and there is no concern of delay, yet preparing them still does not override שבת or יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the two loaves are the obligation of the day, and there is no reason to decree "lest he delay," yet they do not override שבת or יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings his proof. Even the שתי הלחם, which belong to this exact festival, may not be baked on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the שתי הלחם, nobody can delay them, because they are only brought on שבועות. So the ban on baking them on יום טוב cannot be a fence against delay. It must be a Torah rule: anything that could have been done before the festival may not be done on the festival. נדרים ונדבות could also be brought on another day, so they are forbidden by the same Torah rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The two wheat loaves offered on שבועות
An obligation tied to that specific day
Overrides (pushes aside a prohibition)

steps.whatToRemember: According to this view, the Torah only allows on יום טוב what must be done on the festival itself. Anything that could be done earlier or later is forbidden, even for the Temple.
steps.confusionAlert: The point is about baking the loaves. The loaves themselves are still offered on שבועות. They must be baked beforehand, because the baking could have been done before the festival.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם, דְּחוֹבַת הַיּוֹם נִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: For the two loaves, which are an obligation of the day,
and there is no reason to decree lest he delay,
phrases.notes: They can only be brought on שבועות, so delay is impossible.

phrases.english: and yet it does not override שבת
nor יום טוב.
phrases.notes: Their baking must be done before the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for רב הונא's claim in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That the ban on נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב is from the Torah, not a rabbinic fence.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that baking the שתי הלחם does not override שבת or יום טוב, even though the concern of delay does not apply to them.

steps.title: What if someone slaughtered a vow offering on the festival anyway?
steps.stepSummary: The Sages ask what happens, according to the forbidding view, if someone went ahead and slaughtered a נדר or נדבה on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: According to the one who says vow-offerings and gift-offerings are not brought on יום טוב, if someone broke the rule and slaughtered one, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question. If the slaughter already happened against the rule, may the next steps (sprinkling the blood) be done on יום טוב? This sets up two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaughter is already done and cannot be undone. The question is whether the remaining service, sprinkling the blood, may now go forward on יום טוב. To allow it, there must be some festival-related need that justifies it.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (a question posed for discussion)
He transgressed and slaughtered (the act was already done improperly)

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
According to the one who says vow-offerings and gift-offerings
are not brought on a festival,
if he transgressed and slaughtered, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the forbidding view from Steps 14-16 and asks about the case after the fact.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, and why, the blood may be sprinkled on יום טוב after a forbidden slaughter of a נדר or נדבה.

steps.title: רבא: sprinkle the blood so the meat can be eaten
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the blood is sprinkled in order to permit the meat to be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He sprinkles the blood in order to permit the meat to be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the first answer. The blood may be sprinkled, because doing so allows the meat to be eaten on the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat of an offering may not be eaten until the blood is sprinkled. Eating on יום טוב counts as a festival need ("לכם"). That need justifies sprinkling the blood now.

keyTerms.meaning: He sprinkles the blood (on the מזבח)
In order to permit
For eating

phrases.english: Rava said: He sprinkles the blood
in order to permit the meat for eating.
phrases.notes: The meat is eaten on the festival, which is a festival need.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sprinkle the blood, justified by the need to permit the meat for eating on יום טוב.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: sprinkle the blood so the fats can be burned at night
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that the blood is sprinkled in order to burn the אימורין in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: He sprinkles the blood in order to burn the sacrificial parts in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא gives a second answer. He also allows sprinkling, but he bases it on a different purpose: preparing the אימורין to be burned on the מזבח that night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים allow sprinkling the blood, but each gives a different reason. רבא ties it to the meat being eaten on the festival. רבה בר רב הונא ties it to the אימורין, which may only be burned once the blood has been sprinkled and which can be burned in the evening.

keyTerms.meaning: To burn on the מזבח
The sacrificial parts (fats and organs) burned on the מזבח
In the evening

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבא and רבה בר רב הונא agree the blood may be sprinkled after a forbidden slaughter in the ordinary case. They give different reasons: permitting the meat for eating (רבא) or preparing the אימורין for burning at night (רבה בר רב הונא). Those different reasons lead to a practical difference, explained in step 21.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said: He sprinkles the blood
in order to burn the sacrificial parts in the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative reason, different from רבא's in Step 18, for the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sprinkle the blood, justified by the need to burn the אימורין in the evening.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two answers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבא and רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: Both רבא and רבה בר רב הונא said the blood is sprinkled, so the גמרא asks where their reasons would lead to different results. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reason is to permit the meat to be eaten. רבה בר רב הונא's reason is to burn the אימורין in the evening. Since both reach the same ruling in the ordinary case, the גמרא looks for a case where the two reasons split.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? (a request for the practical outcome of a dispute)

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two answers given in steps 18 and 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רבא and רבה בר רב הונא would rule differently.

steps.title: The difference: the meat became impure or was lost
steps.stepSummary: If the meat became טמא or was lost, רבא says not to sprinkle the blood, and רבה בר רב הונא says to sprinkle it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when the meat became impure or was lost. According to רבא, one does not sprinkle. According to רבה בר רב הונא, one does sprinkle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the case where the two opinions split: the meat can no longer be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, sprinkling is only allowed in order to make the meat edible. Once the meat is טמא or lost, that reason is gone, so one may not sprinkle. For רבה בר רב הונא, the reason is to burn the אימורין that evening, and that reason still applies even without the meat, so one does sprinkle.

keyTerms.meaning: The meat became ritually impure (and so may not be eaten)
That it was lost
He sprinkles (the blood on the מזבח)

steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows that each opinion's reason really controls the ruling. That is why the next objection can test רבה בר רב הונא directly.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where the meat became impure or was lost.
According to Rava, he does not sprinkle;
according to Rabba bar Rav Huna, he does sprinkle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ נִטְמָא בָּשָׂר אוֹ שֶׁאָבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the meat is טמא or lost, רבא forbids sprinkling and רבה בר רב הונא permits it.

steps.title: Objection begins: the ברייתא of the כבשי עצרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא as an objection. It rules that if the כבשי עצרת were slaughtered for the wrong purpose or at the wrong time, the blood is still sprinkled and the meat is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: The lambs of שבועות that one slaughtered not for their own purpose, or that one slaughtered either before their time or after their time, the blood is sprinkled and the meat is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a ברייתא to challenge רבה בר רב הונא. This part only gives the weekday rule and sets up the key clause about שבת that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These lambs were slaughtered שלא לשמן or at the wrong time. They are still valid offerings, even though the community has not fulfilled its obligation with them. On an ordinary day their blood is sprinkled and their meat is eaten, as with any valid offering. The challenge will come from what the ברייתא says about שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a תנאי source)
The two lambs brought as שלמים with the שתי הלחם on שבועות
Not for their own purpose (slaughtered with intent for a different offering)
Their proper time

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not for their own purpose' does not make these lambs invalid. They are still kosher offerings. They just do not count for the community's שבועות obligation.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The lambs of Shavuot that one slaughtered not for their own purpose,
or that one slaughtered either before their time
or after their time —
the blood is sprinkled and the meat is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test רבה בר רב הונא's ruling from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא, who allows sprinkling in order to burn the אימורין even when the meat cannot be eaten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא is being set up to show a case where sprinkling is forbidden even though the אימורין could still be offered.

steps.title: On שבת the blood is not sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if it was שבת, one does not sprinkle the blood. It then begins the case of someone who sprinkled anyway, and the text breaks off there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it was שבת, he does not sprinkle. And if he sprinkled —
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the key clause: on שבת these lambs' blood is not sprinkled. It then starts to say what happens if someone sprinkled anyway, and that sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, sprinkling these lambs' blood would not serve their מצוה or any other need. Even so, the ברייתא does not allow sprinkling just so the אימורין can be offered. This seems to work against רבה בר רב הונא, and the next passage completes the objection.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not sprinkle
And if he did sprinkle (after the fact)

steps.confusionAlert: The step stops in the middle of a sentence. Do not try to draw the conclusion yet. What happens 'if he sprinkled' is the next line of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: And if it was Shabbat, he does not sprinkle.
And if he sprinkled —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the שבת clause, which is the core of the objection.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If sprinkling to allow the אימורין to be offered were reason enough, the ברייתא should permit it on שבת. Instead it forbids it, and the next passage will develop this objection.
